title: A Survey on Large Language Models for Critical Societal Domains: Finance, Healthcare, and Law

bias_targets.methodology: The survey reviews literature (such as the Financial Bias Indicators framework) that evaluates the financial rationality of LLMs, specifically measuring belief bias and risk preference bias in financial decision-making tasks.

The paper reviews existing studies that evaluate LLMs for social stereotypes and discrimination against demographic groups (specifically noting race, gender, and disability) by analyzing open-ended dialogue generation and model outputs.

The survey examines literature on fairness in high-stakes legal and financial contexts, noting how models are evaluated for anti-discrimination based on economic status, political status, and crime history in tasks like loan approval and legal sentencing.

The paper reviews studies that identify and measure monolingual bias, evaluating how language models exhibit unfairness or performance degradation when processing languages different from their primary training corpora.
